test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 29 Oct, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: In which of the following cities of India was the first successful textile mill established?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Mumbai**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The first successful **textile mill** in India was established in **Mumbai** in the year **1854**.
 
• Mumbai emerged as the ideal location for the establishment of the textile mill due to its proximity to the **cotton-growing areas** in western India, particularly in Maharashtra.
 
• The availability of a **port** in Mumbai facilitated the import of machinery and export of finished goods, making it a strategic location for textile production.
 
• The mill was founded by a **Parsee entrepreneur**, Cowasji Nanabhai Davar, and was called the **Bombay Spinning and Weaving Company**.
 
• Mumbai became known as the **Manchester of India** due to its dominance in the textile industry during the British era.
 
• The establishment of the first textile mill marked the beginning of the **industrial revolution** in India and set the stage for the growth of the textile industry across the country.
 
• The textile industry in Mumbai played a significant role in boosting employment and contributing to the **economic development** of the region.
 
• It laid the foundation for **modern industries** in India and encouraged other industrial activities in the region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Chennai**__

 __
 
• **Chennai**, also known as Madras, is an important industrial hub in southern India but was not the location for the first successful textile mill.
 
• It is known for its **automobile and software industries**, as well as traditional industries like leather and textiles.
 
• Chennai has a rich history of cotton textile production, but its prominence came later compared to Mumbai.
 
 
 
• **Lucknow**__
 __
 
• **Lucknow**, the capital city of Uttar Pradesh, is renowned for its traditional **Chikankari embroidery**, which is a hand-embroidery technique.
 
• It is not historically associated with the establishment of large-scale textile mills during the industrial revolution era.
 
• Lucknow's contributions to textiles are more focused on traditional crafts rather than modern textile mills.
 
 
 
• **Kolkata**__
 
 
• **Kolkata**, formerly known as Calcutta, was an important commercial center during British rule but was not the site of the first textile mill.
 
• The city is known for its **jute industry**, with the first jute mill established in the late 19th century.
 
• Kolkata has a long history of industrial activity but was more prominent in industries like jute and tea rather than cotton textiles during the initial stages of industrialization in India.
